findings.reason: either §3 must declare a session-aware simulation as its deliverable or §9 must restate that arm against the live lane, and until one of those is chosen the node extends a done section or fails its gate.
findings.text: §9's second arm requires "the §3 simulation" to run one session with an unbounded queue beside four sessions holding one worker each and compares the result with the same workload as a single session, but §2 records that "reckon's per-session shares and holds bound the live worker count in ways the simulation does not carry" and the prototype `sim.py` models one lane-wide admission rule with no session grouping, while §3's deliverable only requires the router's slot rule to be called and never names per-session allocation — so the arm measures something the instrument the plan declares cannot produce, and a worker reads it as either an undispatched extension of §3 or a check it must fake

findings.reason: the worker must choose between honouring §4's record (21 free, negative control no longer reproducing the starvation) and honouring the stated input (7 free, per-session and lane-wide counts disagreeing as they do today), and neither passes as written.
findings.text: the unit test is specified as "a capacity of 32 with five sessions holding 6, 1, 2, 1 and 1 live runs and 7 free slots", but under §4's rule the lanes' free slots are capacity less the lane-wide live runs, so 11 live runs at capacity 32 leave 21 free, and 7 free is reachable only with the 25-run lane-wide count the same section forbids the per-session block to disagree with — the negative control "the same input with one reserve held per session offers the session holding 6 nothing" also needs that stale count, since four per-session reserves of 2 leave 13 of 21 slots to the session at its share and would not starve it at all
